passages.title: Not quite a birthday feast
passages.text: Last month my father turned fifty, and I offered to cook a special dinner for the whole family. I had watched lots of cooking programmes, so I was sure it would be easy. How wrong I was! First, I found out that we did not have (1) ______ eggs at all, so I had to run to the corner shop. While I was out, the cheese sauce boiled for (2) ______ long that it turned into a thick brown paste. Then I added salt to the rice twice by mistake, and it became (3) ______ salty for anyone to eat. When Dad came home, the kitchen was full of smoke and there was nothing on the table at all, apart (4) ______ a plate of burnt bread. Luckily, he just laughed. We opened all the windows and walked to the little Italian restaurant (5) ______ my parents had their first date many years ago. The pizza was delicious. Afterwards, (6) ______ took us nearly two hours to clean the kitchen, but Dad said it was the most memorable birthday he had ever had.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: In a negative sentence we use any with plural nouns: "we did not have any eggs at all". The words at all show that the answer is any, not some or many.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: So + adverb + that shows a result: the sauce boiled "for so long that it turned into a thick brown paste". Too or very cannot be followed by a that-clause of result.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: The pattern is too + adjective + for someone + to-infinitive: the rice became "too salty for anyone to eat". So or very cannot be followed by for anyone to eat.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: Apart from means except: "nothing on the table at all, apart from a plate of burnt bread". Apart is always followed by from in this meaning.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: Where introduces a relative clause about a place: "the little Italian restaurant where my parents had their first date". Which or that would need at at the end of the clause.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: The pattern for time needed is it + take + time + to-infinitive: "it took us nearly two hours to clean the kitchen". The subject must be the empty pronoun it.
